title: An Agora only exists when people show up
content:
On the morning of 29 October, two weeks after the Irish Presidency of the Council of the EU presented a negotiation box proposing a 30% cut to AgoraEU, a wave of pink energy and joyful anger stormed Schuman Square, reclaiming it as what an agora should be: a space for people to gather and speak up.

AgoraEU is the future EU funding programme for culture, media and civil society, and the proposal to cut it by almost a third comes at a time when its share of the EU budget already amounts to just a tiny fraction of the whole. 

Cutting AgoraEU means fewer books, films and performances, fewer independent investigations, and less support for the people and organisations defending our rights. In short, it means less space for the voices, stories and ideas that bring our democracies to life. 

In response to this dreadful scenario, together with our partners and friends at Civil Society Europe, European Civic Forum, the European Federation of Journalists, and in the Future of Europe cohort, we called on the cultural, media and civil society sectors to stand up for AgoraEU. 

And we did. Marvelously, and in full pink.
